svg.text: From a map cell to the screen: the three address spaces round_scroll_step walks for map row r, column c

g.text: the collision map, $E398
32 rows x 16 bytes, a nibble per cell
row r: byte $E398 + 16 r
cell c: byte + c/2, high nibble if c is even
0 = solid
video RAM, playfield A: $CD00-$D4FF
32 tile columns of 64 bytes (a 2-byte cell per row)
tile column c: $CD00 + 64 c
row r: + 2 r (tile number, then attribute)
two tile columns = one 128-byte object column
the object list, entries 0-15
one strip per object column $1A-$29
strip s = c / 2: entry s at $E1CD + 4 s
[line, $DB + s, 0, bank]: chained x, 16 px each
line byte: 0 at rest, + 2 per frame of the scroll
nibble 0 ->
plain wall tile
64 bytes ->
one tile column
Per map row, three passes over the 32 cells:
1 scroll_clear_column zero the row's 32 cells
2 scroll_draw_walls nibble 0 -> the round's plain block (tile base + 4, colour group 14 or 15 by round parity)
3 scroll_shade_walls an empty cell with a plain block above and/or to the left gets one of the edge tiles $F0-$F5
4 scroll_cap_columns two rows behind: the two border columns' plain blocks become the 2 x 2 pattern (tiles base + 0..3)
The clear-and-draw runs on the row that has just left the top of the strips, which are 256-line rings: the row comes back in at the bottom
carrying the next round. The status row rides on playfield B's sixteen fixed strips for the 128 frames of the scroll, and moves back afterwards.
